Note this cost-based lookback-5 survivor set differs from the prior lookback-robust set (which had MSFT at all three lookbacks and JPM REGIME_DEPENDENT): under cost, MSFT's lookback-5 verdict becomes REGIME_DEPENDENT (it still survives at lookbacks 3/10, so remains COST_ROBUST overall) while JPM's lookback-5 becomes REGIME_STABLE. Conclusion: the short-horizon momentum edge is not a turnover/cost artifact under the repository's cost model.
preceding_agent.question: Does the short-horizon momentum edge survive conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected real-data universe?
preceding_agent.research_result: The short-horizon momentum edge survives conservative transaction-cost stress on the 10-asset collected universe under the repository's existing realistic cost model and matched coin-flip null. Candidate-only: 9/10 positive at zero and conservative cost, none eroded (max shift <= 0.002 for 8/10; 0.05 for NVDA, already NO_EDGE). Verdict-based: COST_ROBUST=7, COST_FRAGILE=0, NO_EDGE=3 (NVDA, JNJ, XOM); lookback-5 survives conservative 6/10 (AAPL, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA, JPM; note MSFT's lookback-5 is REGIME_DEPENDENT under cost but it survives at lookbacks 3/10 so remains COST_ROBUST overall). Independently verified (4 gates MATCH, fresh path) and deterministic; 168/168 regression tests pass. Qualification: the result is specific to the repo's constant-dollar + per-share-commission model; a bps-only stress and a strict temporal holdout remain untested. This is a positive qualification that strengthens (does not overturn) the admitted candidate; it is not a new strategy and not a negative result.
preceding_agent.uncertainty_reduced: Reduced uncertainty that the momentum candidate is a cost artifact: under the repo's realistic and 2x conservative cost model the candidate's positive P&L is essentially unchanged for the 6 lookback-robust assets and no asset's positive candidate is eroded by cost (independently verified, deterministic). Did NOT resolve behavior under a pure bps-only cost model or a strict temporal holdout; those are recorded as open.
preceding_agent.uncertainty_targeted: Whether the short-horizon (lookback 3/5/10) momentum edge survives conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected universe, or is a gross-of-cost turnover artifact of daily rebalancing.
unverified: The repository has no single frozen 'realistic cost model' constant; the canonical model from examples/ma_crossover*.py was used plus a 2x conservative stress. Other venues/exchange-fee schedules and a pure percent-of-notional (bps-only) cost model were NOT tested.

Under constant-dollar sizing the per-bar rebalancing cost is small relative to the edge for medium/high-priced assets, so the test is more sensitive to the per-share commission on low-priced assets (NVDA) than to a uniform bps drag; a bps-only cost stress is a complementary check that remains open.

The identical-across-lookbacks candidate medians are a pre-established framework property (activation 37394344201 horizon analysis), not re-derived here.

No strict temporal holdout (select on early data, evaluate the most-recent untouched period once) was run; all walk-forward folds reuse the full sample, so a true out-of-sample holdout remains untested.
